set.body:
Context: review of the latent encoding/decoding and archive modules found a good typed Scala 3 core, but several public contracts still fall back to raw maps, strings, metadata conventions, or Option-shaped absence where domain ADTs would make illegal states harder to express.

Goal: harden the latent/archive API into a more idiomatic object-functional Scala 3 surface while preserving archive wire compatibility and the existing JVM/JS roundtrip proof.

Acceptance criteria:
- Latent metadata and labels are carried as validated domain types end-to-end; raw Map[String,String] remains a wire/interoperability boundary, not the internal model.
- Archive variant identity is represented by a typed descriptor algebra instead of relying on incidental metadata-string conventions.
- Decode/reconstruct semantics explicitly distinguish linear coefficient decoding, affine offsets, residual/event payloads, and full materialization.
- Capability/absence states are modeled with sealed ADTs where Option currently hides domain meaning.
- Temporal specs such as DctSpec and HaarSpec remain valid-by-construction and gain value-like ergonomics.
- LatentArchiveCodec is split into family-sized interpreters without changing readable/writable archive semantics.
- Focused JVM and Scala.js tests prove compatibility and representative roundtrips after each slice.
set.title: Epic: Latent/archive typed surface hardening
